_comment: The claims file (#915 Wave 3). It replaces tests/claims.json and holds ONLY what a machine cannot derive: the qualities x surfaces vocabulary, the lane registry, the 45 claim rows with their severity and the date each was last demonstrated red, the law registry, the consent ledger, the join laws, the deliberate n/a cells with their reasons, and the flow ownership + minimumTests floors. Owners, journeys, budgets, seeds, engines, fuzz targets and Vitest projects are DERIVED at read time by scripts/test-report/derive.mjs from the roster, the Stryker configs, scripts/mutation/seeds.mjs, scripts/fuzz/targets.mjs and vitest.config.ts — see TESTING.md.
_why: tests/claims.json was 252 KB of hand-typed grid whose per-cell assessments duplicated what the lanes already proved. #915 keeps the declarations (a claim, a law, a reason for an absence) and derives the observations.

severity.S2: Silent wrongness — the product does the wrong thing and says nothing.
severity.S3: A promise degraded — slower, noisier, or partly unproven.
severity.S4: Fidelity, or blocked on something outside the repo.

consent-denial-monotone.statement: Withdrawing a standing answer, replacing it with a declined row, or narrowing a clamp verb can only turn an allow into a deny, never a deny into an allow.

consent-clamp-order-independent.statement: The decision, the set of returned rowFilter clauses, and the fieldMask are invariant under permutation of identity.scopeClamp.

consent-clamp-only-narrows.statement: For every allow, the returned rowFilter is exactly the covering clamp scopes' clauses and the fieldMask exactly their intersection (null only when every covering scope leaves it null); a standing answer contributes no rows and no fields of its own.

consent-reveal-never-rides.statement: No standing answer ever confers reveal, so an automation is refused reveal whatever it holds; a clamp scope carrying only 'reveal' satisfies no read or act request.

consent-standing-answer-required.statement: No caller but the owner's own device reaches anything without a live granted share_authority row covering the entity for the verb, and naming a first-party surface confers nothing: a surface identity reaches exactly what the bare owner device reaches.

consent-onbehalf-cap-precedes-grants.statement: When onBehalfOfOwner.mayAct is false, no standing answer produces an allow for act or reveal, and the deny names the owner id, checked before any answer is consulted.

untrusted-display-total.statement: displayText never throws for any input (non-strings included), preserves code-point length and is idempotent for strings, and emits no character in the forbidden C0-control/DEL/bidi-override/bidi-isolate set.

untrusted-url-allowlist-closed.statement: safeExternalUrl/safeMediaUrl/safeDocumentUrl each return null or a value in that function's own scheme allowlist, never matching javascript:/vbscript:/data:text/html/data:image/svg; safeExternalUrl additionally never returns a value carrying a control code unit (<=32 or 127).

untrusted-media-subsumed-by-document.statement: Every value safeMediaUrl accepts, safeDocumentUrl accepts with an identical result; the converse (document accepts, media rejects) occurs only for data:application/pdf and data:text/plain.

untrusted-background-image-unescapable.statement: safeBackgroundImage output is undefined or a single sealed CSS url("…") token whose every quote and backslash is escaped and which recovers exactly the URL the media sink admitted, so no member string can break out of the quoted string.

commons-steward-ordered-convergence.statement: Each Commons grant has one independent monotonic steward sequence; cursor-gapped members converge to the same domain state, and capability downgrades govern commands from their exact stream position onward.

placement-registry-parity.statement: Every placeable blueprint entity is enumerated once and Locker is structurally excluded.

pending-overlay.statement: Every blueprint local read is replica plus durable outbox, with per-action projection declarations and structural exclusions owned by one engine.

custody-seat-exclusion.statement: Record-only blueprint apps never import or render byte-custody machinery.

consent-domain-parity.statement: Blueprint consent surfaces and automation scheduling recognize the same enrichment domains.

triage-session-progress.statement: Proposal queues share frozen progress, distinct skip semantics, and reachable completion.

search-scaffold-grouping.statement: Search entity configuration owns grouping, ordering, caps, and result-state truth.

per-scope-reach.statement: Every mounted scope reports whether search reached it, was offline, or refused the query instead of collapsing those states into no matches.

mask-refuses-not-no-matches.statement: A field-masked search refusal remains a typed refusal through the replica and search-scaffold boundary and is never rendered as an honest empty result.

recognition-self-contained.statement: Blueprint apps, automations, and mobile code use host-owned model seams and never resurrect provider SDKs or deleted inference roads.

provider-egress-dispatch.statement: Outbound provider requests leave centraid only through the ACP dispatch path — runTurn resolving a HARNESSES spec and spawning it via harnessSpawnEnv, downstream of decideEnrichmentGate — never through a provider SDK import, a provider API host literal, or a host-path HTTP client.

one-computation.statement: A pure product-law computation is a projection or a shared module imported by every seat, never two seat-local implementations.

app-entity-tripwire.statement: Every entity a bundled app's queries, actions and phone screens read, and every command they invoke, is declared in that app's app.json#vault.scopes — minimisation is a build-time check over the manifest, not a runtime grant evaluation (#928 A1).

select-all-filtered.statement: Select-all takes the rows the current filter shows, never the whole table, and a selection survives a filter change through pruneSelection rather than being carried onto rows the member never saw.

people-photograph-counts.statement: Every seat counts distinct confirmed photographs, not face regions or unconfirmed proposals, and keeps unnamed groups separate.

enrichment-model-lock.statement: Every live-model file and native runtime dependency is immutable by version/digest and its permissive licence is recorded in LICENSES.md.

enrichment-live.statement: Pinned real weights satisfy the advertised capability/model handshake and the committed OCR, embedding, and face-geometry goldens.

backup-round-trip.statement: A restored snapshot reproduces the vault byte-identically — same files, same directory tree, plus the quarantine marker.

backup-incremental.statement: A second snapshot after a small change uploads far fewer chunks than the first, so backup cost tracks change, not vault size.

backup-no-change.statement: A run over an unchanged vault registers nothing and returns null, so an idle machine never mints snapshots.

backup-restore-refusal.statement: Restore refuses a non-empty destination, a newer vaultUserVersion, an unknown format, and a manifest whose hash does not verify — and refuses before fetching or materializing anything.

backup-verify.statement: Verification detects a deleted chunk and a corrupted chunk, and reports a clean snapshot as clean.

share-closure-confinement.statement: A share closure carries only the rows reachable from the items it names — no other row, derivative or blob of the origin vault crosses — and an item the origin does not hold refuses the whole read rather than yielding a partial closure.

share-receipt-authority.statement: A cross-vault access receipt exists exactly when a placement's rows landed at the audience, naming the authorised origin scope and the audience ids created, once per placement token; a refused placement, one this gateway could not perform, and a malformed scope each leave none.

experimental-gate-parity.statement: An experimental feature is advertised in the C1 handshake exactly when its own routes are mounted: gated off it is absent from capabilities and its surfaces are unowned; gated on, and only then, they answer.

insights-rollup-render-or-withhold.statement: Every field of the gateway's insights rollup is rendered on Analytics or withheld on the record with a stated reason; a field that is neither is a silent deletion.

native-block-flag-marks.statement: Every semantic flag the shared block contracts declare produces a mark on the phone that the unflagged form does not — accepting a flag and drawing the ordinary control is not parity.

people-overdue-never.statement: Cadence 0 is Never and never overdue.

people-link-tristate.statement: The link fact is linked, unlinked, or absent — never a false unlinked on a denied share read.

people-roster-sub.statement: A linked roster row's second line leads with Linked, then the role if any.

people-trash-split.statement: Deleted profiles are the trash shelf, not roster rows, and carry purge_at.

people-search-scope.statement: People search covers name, role and notes.

people-avatar-hue.statement: A stored avatar hue round-trips as a wheel key, honours a hex verbatim, and otherwise derives from the party id.

people-link-ring.statement: The avatar ring states the link and only the link: solid when linked, dashed when unlinked, nothing when unknown.

people-row-marks.statement: The People row's meta takes net only as a consequence of being overdue.

people-star-a11y.statement: The star names its person and its direction.

people-readonly-star.statement: A person in a read-only source withholds the star: the press is refused instead of letting the write throw, the control reports itself disabled and carries the reason, and it still names Star or Unstar.

people-row-pending.statement: A queued People change says so on its own row: the overlay sentence is a third line under the sub, and a row with no pending change draws no pending line at all.

pending-destructive-projection.statement: Every destructive action the eight blueprint apps declare projects a delete or a tombstone while its intent is queued, or carries a written structural exclusion; a plain patch that leaves the row on screen is a finding.

consentLedger.label: Vault consent gateway
consentLedger.note: The closed deny set every seat inherits; the contract suite exercises it, no generated denial sweep does.

consentLedger.label: App scope manifests
consentLedger.note: The G4 sweep landed (#839): manifest-scope-denial.{sweep,closed-grammar,fuzz} drive the real validateManifest + parseManifest + evaluateAccess over all 37 bundled manifests — every declared scope×verb allows, every undeclared combination denies closed inside the six DENY_CLASSES, and property fuzz holds. #864 M5 adds manifest-scope-denial.hostile: synthetic third-party/attacker manifests built in memory and pushed through the real validators — case, NFKC, whitespace and __proto__/constructor name variants and a 10000-scope list deny as manifest-undeclared, and the validator layer refuses malformed shapes (a garbage rowFilter op the app schema waves through is rejected by the automation validator). Open hole characterized by test.fails + a filed note: the app manifest validator types rowFilter.op as a bare string and executionClamp carries rowFilter/fieldMask contents opaquely, so a structurally-invalid clause reaches ALLOW and is refused only as a bare throw at filters.ts compile, outside the receipt grammar.

consentLedger.label: Grant plane
consentLedger.note: Create/revoke/fulfil and the view|edit capability split are owned; revocation PROPAGATION across seats is not (gap G2, #839 Wave 3).

consentLedger.label: Enrichment egress policy
consentLedger.note: The cascade and the egress ceiling fail closed on undefined; example-based only, no property suite over the fold (#839 Wave 2).

consentLedger.label: Enrichment consent surface
consentLedger.note: The closed ENRICH_DOMAINS union and the on-device/off-device answer split; mobile draws its own consent surface.

consentLedger.label: Device sessions and pairing
consentLedger.note: Pairing tickets and session revocation sever both planes; the contract suite owns it.

consentLedger.label: OS device permissions
consentLedger.refusalGrammar: the OS grant is read, never assumed; a denied grant renders the app's denied state rather than an empty library
consentLedger.note: Gap G8: one of eight apps has a device flow; contacts, biometrics and notification grants are unowned (#839 Wave 4).

consentLedger.label: Provider egress ban
consentLedger.refusalGrammar: structural — the ban is an import-graph law, so there is no refusal string to say
consentLedger.note: The SDK-import ban is owned by [law:recognition-self-contained]; the dispatch-path law is gap G5 (#839 Wave 2).

joinLaws.label: Grant delivery is addressed
joinLaws.testName: a grant crosses mounted vaults over the real transport, and only the addressed seat receives it
joinLaws.statement: A grant fulfilled on one mounted vault reaches exactly the addressed seat over the real wire; every other joined seat sees nothing.

joinLaws.label: Revocation severs, never pauses
joinLaws.testName: revocation propagates across the join and severs delivery, not merely pauses it
joinLaws.statement: Revoking a grant propagates across the join and ends delivery to the revoked seat; a paused-but-resumable stream is a failure, not a pass.

joinLaws.label: Parked writes settle once
joinLaws.testName: a parked payload survives a transport reconnect, then settles once and never unparks
joinLaws.statement: A payload parked before a transport drop survives the reconnect and settles exactly once; it never returns to parked afterwards.

joinLaws.label: Version skew meets one wall
joinLaws.testName: an N-1 client meets one update wall over the real transport, with no fallback mode
joinLaws.statement: An out-of-window client joining the gateway is refused with one update wall and no degraded fallback mode.

joinLaws.label: Schedules replay from their seed
joinLaws.testName: the same seed produces the same program
joinLaws.statement: A seeded interleaving is a program: the same seed yields the same schedule, so a simulation failure is replayable rather than anecdotal.

joinLaws.label: The grant plane replays too
joinLaws.testName: the grant plane replays from its seed too
joinLaws.statement: The grant plane rides the same seeded schedule as the commons rail, and a run that proved nothing about grants is itself a failure.

joinLaws.label: Every seed converges
joinLaws.testName: seed %i converges and holds every golden invariant
joinLaws.statement: Across the pinned seed set — including the regression seeds earlier runs found — cursor-gapped members converge and every golden invariant holds through pulls, crash-restarts and compaction.

joinLaws.label: Five seats, three grants, heavy overlap
joinLaws.testName: a five-seat, three-grant world with heavy overlap also converges
joinLaws.statement: Widening the world past the join lane's floor — five seats sharing three overlapping grants — does not break convergence.

joinLaws.label: Grant lifecycle interleaves with the rail
joinLaws.testName: seed 839001 interleaves the grant lifecycle with the commons rail
joinLaws.statement: Grant create / fulfil / origin-edit operations interleaved with commons traffic on one seeded schedule still converge to one domain state.

joinLaws.label: Revocation severs a grant the host lost reach for
joinLaws.testName: a revocation severs a grant the host lost reach for mid-life
joinLaws.statement: A grant whose delivered fulfillment degraded to syncing because the host lost reach is still severed by a revocation, rather than settled as removed while the audience keeps the projection.
